title: Rectangle sign equals Boolean sign on leaf rectangles
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Boolean output, over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob). If $R$ is a leaf rectangle of $p$ and $(x, y)$ is any point of $R$, then the rectangle sign of $R$ agrees with the Boolean sign of the value that $p$ computes on $(x, y)$: it equals $+1$ when $p$ outputs $\mathrm{false}$ at $(x, y)$ and $-1$ when $p$ outputs $\mathrm{true}$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic protocol with Boolean output
R is a leaf rectangle of p
replaced:
If $R$ is a leaf rectangle of protocol $p$ and $(x,y) \in R$, then
$\mathrm{rectangleSign}(p,R) = \sigma(p.\mathrm{run}(x,y))$, where $\sigma$ is the sign
map \texttt{CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}.
